page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-16 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores, with multithreading delivering two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB, establishing an elevated ratio of 8 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache resources comprise 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Standard instruction extensions include AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent. The platform includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core throughput placing in the top 25 percent at 2682.69 points. Multithreaded computational output is balanced, yielding a multi-core stress-ng result of 21541.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9162.0. Memory subsystems deliver 100.27 GB/s read bandwidth and 54.01 GB/s write bandwidth on 256 MB blocks, supporting 15.76 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.4 GB/s static web serving throughput. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for persistent data needs.

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of the E2 architecture, providing a cost-effective allocation of high RAM volume without demanding premium compute-tier pricing. Given its high memory-to-CPU configuration, the e2-highmem-16 is best suited for memory-bound workloads, including distributed caching layers, Redis deployments, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-heavy batch processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 128 GB of RAM, offering a generous 8 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no discrete GPUs and relies entirely on external network storage, as zero local disk space is bundled. In benchmark assessments, it achieves upper-quartile single-core CPU throughput alongside reliable mid-tier multi-core execution, demonstrated by a 15.76 million operations per second Redis SET throughput. Offering strong resource density for RAM-intensive tasks without the cost profile of specialized bare-metal hardware, the e2-highmem-16 is suitable for in-memory key-value stores, intermediate data caching, relational databases, and enterprise data processing workloads.
